verdicts.reason: Quote only describes a fixed design property (32-bit data width, no parameter). There is no behaviour to verify or stimulus to exercise; it is a structural description, not a testable requirement.

Quote says values outside 16 to 32 are illegal, so the prohibition is correct. It is a configuration constraint, not checkable every cycle from interface signals, so check=none is wrong. A scenario can cover the legal range boundaries (16 and 32) and confirm that illegal values are never used.

questions.question: Section 8 is referenced for illegal PARA_ADDR_W values. What does the design do if one is configured (elaboration error, undefined behaviour, or silent clamp)? This decides whether illegal values can be tested at all.
